clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1991–1992
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather's death in June 1991, within months: you leaned hard on Rafe and then clashed with him once a wrist injury stopped your playing in October; you were on your own, getting high, absorbed in fixing radios by November; by January 1992 you were lost and low, unable to get going, with your grandfather gone and your mother about to remarry. Your mother filled in your college forms in March, and by autumn you were in a bleak year at the community college, nights out playing pool, days asleep. In January 1994 you were stung that your dad had never heard of the film you were making. These shifts in your functioning and your moves toward and away from people cluster around the loss and the household changes that followed.

clusters.name: Your grandfather Clifford's return to the family, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Your grandfather Clifford came back into the family after years away in 1989, within months of which your stepfather took a rental on Quarry Lane and you settled in the rebuilt Hollin Road house that autumn. You liked late nights and dropped chess and debate club. Your sister Tara was born in July 1990. Across these years: your mother filled in your college forms; you began at the conservatory, hurt your wrist in the first term, clashed with your roommate Rafe, got high absorbed in radios, and were lost and low by early 1992; your grandfather Gordon died in June 1991 and your grandmother Winifred was treated for a thyroid tumour. You spent a bleak year at the community college; you found your drive again with an exchange in Portugal and raced through your degree. Your cousin Bella was treated for melanoma. These shifts across the years—your symptom up, your functioning down then up, your moves toward your father and away from people—cluster around the wider family's stirring and the household's rebuilding.

clusters.name: Your move to Gull Harbour and the years after, 2002–2004
clusters.reason: Around September 2002 when you moved to Gull Harbour, you were on poor terms with family and friends, with no footing as your performing career was running out of steam. That winter you met Marisol at a party and moved to Fenwick with her by June 2003. When you split within the year you sank into a deep depression that took hold that winter once you were back in Thornbury, hardly moving from the sofa. You could not face your family; you relied, gingerly, on friends. By January 2004 you began swimming laps and requested help from your parents with therapy costs, and returned to your therapist. Around these same months, starting in September 2001, your grandmother Winifred was found to have bowel cancer and underwent operations then chemotherapy; you had a disastrous audition for the national orchestra in your home town and were done with performing. Your grandmother died of the cancer in February 2004. Your anxiety was up, your functioning down then gradually up; your distance from family shifted to moves toward help and toward friends.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Your grandmother Lorna died in January 2008. Around that time: you spent four weeks building with Silas at Alder Creek before nursing school; you were too drained for conversation with your mother, though she pressed to visit and you kept the door shut on her. Once you moved to Marlow Sound for nursing school in September 2008 you stopped speaking to your mother; the silence held for roughly a year. Your aunt Imogen had a stroke with months of rehabilitation in early 2009. Your partner's brother Leo's first child was born in August 2010. Your distance from your mother and your moves toward friends and toward help clustered around the loss and the upheaval of leaving for nursing school.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your wedding to Wren in March 2017, within months: you saw your mother a bit less once Wren came along. Your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in October 2017. Your sister Tara had a baby on the way, Russell's first grandchild that Jonah knows of, due in late 2019. Your partner's brother Leo and his family returned to Danfield in August 2019. In October 2019 your partner was swamped with one thing after another—a street party, a fundraising dinner, then the drive to the lake for her mother's retirement party. You were too strict laying out a plan to settle her; she was fused with her father and brother, all-day talks with nothing happening to one that the others don't hear. She settled once the weekend had a plan and the dinner went well. At the lake weekend you were awake from the small hours with no more sleep and could only pull back as the others rose; you felt you don't belong. Your anxiety and symptom were up, your functioning down then up; your distance from your partner and from her family clustered around the gathering of her family close and your own unease in that closeness.
